payload.summary: New Orleans pulses with a haunting, jazz-infused atmosphere where the spectral echoes of the past linger in every shadowed alley and opulent mansion, amplified by an eclectic soundtrack dominated by the dark, brooding tones of Nick Cave & the Bad Seeds and the industrial grit of Nine Inch Nails. Unlike Atlanta’s more mainstream rock scene, New Orleans’ cultural texture is steeped in voodoo mystique, decadent cuisine at iconic spots like Commander’s Palace, and the eerie allure of Mardi Gras World, creating a perfect breeding ground for supernatural horror.

npc.description: Clad in a faded denim shirt with a patch of the Louisiana flag, Eleanor runs guided tours through the swamp lands, carrying a weathered copy of a 1970s Voodoo Goblins tour poster. Her boots are caked in mud from the trails, and her stories blend local legend with unsettling truths.
npc.quote: If the gators start singin' and the willows whisper, boy, you best be listenin'.
dialogue: You ever been to Mardi Gras World? Seen how they make those masks? Makes you wonder what they hide from us.
The city's got layers, like gumbo — you stir it up too much, you'll burn your mouth on secrets best left untold.
Don't ask me how I know these things — some knowledge ain't meant for daylight.
eats_at: Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport
New Orleans Ernest N. Morial Convention Center

npc.description: Dressed in bell-bottoms and a sequined vest, Marcus runs the underground disco nights at the Fair Grounds Race Course & Slots. His gold chain glints under the dim lights, and he carries a vintage boombox blasting Nick Cave & the Bad Seeds.
npc.quote: In this town, we dance to forget, not to remember.
dialogue: You think Commander's Palace is fancy? Try gettin' past the bouncer at a secret disco under the race track — that's where the real magic happens.
The system's tight, but we slip through the cracks with a beat and a bottle — that's how we survive.
When the bass drops, you feel it in your bones — that's the only truth I trust.
eats_at: New Orleans Ernest N. Morial Convention Center

npc.description: Wrapped in a vibrant purple dress with gold embroidery, Marie runs a small herbalist shop near the bayou, her hair tied back with a red scarf. She brews teas using plants collected from the local wetlands, and her shelves are lined with ancient books and a framed photo of Bobby Brown.
npc.quote: The spirits don't speak in words — they whisper in the wind and show themselves in the shadows.
dialogue: I get my herbs from the bayou — you wouldn't believe what grows in those waters. Some things shouldn't be picked.
Power ain't always in the hands of the few — sometimes it's in the roots, the leaves, the things folk know but don't say.
When you're alone with the night and the insects, you learn to listen — that's when the truth comes out.
